case_name: Bone et al. v. University of North Carolina Health Care System
court: U.S. District Court, Middle District of North Carolina
industry_specific: University health system — hospitals and outpatient clinics
defendant_name: University of North Carolina Health Care System (UNC Health)
claim_type: ADA Title III and Rehabilitation Act Section 504 — systematic failure to provide written materials (after-visit summaries, billing, medication instructions, patient forms) in accessible formats (Braille, large print, accessible electronic) to blind patients
estimated_costs: $125,000 damages + plaintiff attorney fees + mandatory injunction compliance costs (enterprise-wide accessible communications overhaul)

violation_source_evidence: Disability Rights North Carolina press release (disabilityrightsnc.org, July 14 2022): UNC Health 'provided information critical to the health of their patients in standard print only, without a statutorily required accessible alternative.' Specific inaccessible materials: patient history forms, after-visit summaries, billing information, and general written communications — provided exclusively in standard print with no Braille, large print, or accessible electronic formats. Clearinghouse.net case summary: MyChart online health portal disputed as 'not sufficiently accessible' for blind patients.
summary_one_line: NFB and Disability Rights NC won a $125,000 settlement against UNC Health (2022) for systematically denying blind patients accessible medical records, billing, and forms; a 2023 federal injunction then required a system-wide overhaul of patient communications.
notes: Plaintiffs were Timothy Miles, John Bone, the National Federation of the Blind, and Disability Rights NC. Filed 2018, partial settlement on damages ($125K) reached July 2022. After damages settled, litigation continued on injunctive relief. In June 2023, judge issued a 109-page order and permanent injunction requiring UNC Health to ensure all patient communications are accessible to blind patients. This is a 5-year case showing sustained litigation pressure on healthcare providers. The injunction required electronic records, patient portals, after-visit summaries, billing statements, and all communications to be accessible. Strong precedent for post-2024 HHS Section 504 enforcement.
